incidents.summary: Pearson agreed to pay a $1 million SEC penalty for misleading disclosures about a cyber intrusion that stole millions of student records and administrator credentials.

sources.title: SEC.gov | SEC Charges Pearson Plc for Misleading Investors About Cyber Breach
sources.quote: The SEC's order finds that Pearson made misleading statements and omissions about the 2018 data breach involving the theft of student data and administrator log-in credentials of 13,000 school, district and university customer accounts.

sources.title: SEC.gov | SEC Charges Pearson Plc for Misleading Investors About Cyber Breach
sources.quote: The media statement also omitted that millions of rows of student data and usernames and hashed passwords were stolen.

sources.title: SEC.gov | SEC Charges Pearson Plc for Misleading Investors About Cyber Breach
sources.quote: Without admitting or denying the SEC's findings, Pearson agreed to cease and desist from committing violations of these provisions and to pay a $1 million civil penalty.

incidents.summary: Ofqual imposed a £1.2 million penalty on Pearson in 2022 for failures in GCSE and A-level marking reviews between 2016 and 2019.

sources.title: Pearson plc
sources.quote: In 2022, Ofqual imposed a £1.2 million monetary penalty on Pearson for failures in reviews of marking for GCSE and A-level qualifications between 2016 and 2019.

incidents.summary: Ofqual fined Pearson £750,000 over PTE Academic Online after insufficiently prompt action against candidate malpractice, and Pearson revoked 9,910 affected results.

sources.title: Pearson plc
sources.quote: The penalties were £750,000 for GCSE English language 2.0, £505,000 for A-level Chinese, and £750,000 for Pearson PTE Academic Online.

sources.title: Pearson plc
sources.quote: In the PTE case, Ofqual said Pearson had failed to act sufficiently promptly when candidate malpractice affected delivery of the online version of its secure English-language test; Pearson later revoked 9,910 affected results.

incidents.summary: Ofqual fined Pearson £750,000 in December 2025 for serious breaches involving GCSE English language 2.0.

sources.title: Pearson plc
sources.quote: In December 2025, Ofqual fined Pearson more than £2 million for serious breaches in three separate cases between 2019 and 2023, which the regulator said collectively affected tens of thousands of students.

sources.title: Pearson plc
sources.quote: The penalties were £750,000 for GCSE English language 2.0, £505,000 for A-level Chinese, and £750,000 for Pearson PTE Academic Online.

incidents.summary: More than 61% of shareholders opposed Pearson's remuneration report after its chief executive received about £1.5 million, including a bonus, following a £2.6 billion pre-tax loss.

sources.title: Pearson plc
sources.quote: Chief executive John Fallon received total pay of about £1.5 million, including a bonus, after Pearson reported a pre-tax loss of £2.6 billion for 2016.

sources.title: Pearson plc
sources.quote: At the company's annual general meeting in May 2017, more than 61% of shareholders voted against the remuneration report.

positives: SLR undertook independent limited assurance of Pearson's FY2025 greenhouse-gas and other ESG data.
